Agents and skills

What Claude Code loads from .claude/ in this repository: the commands you run, the agent team they lead, and the standards the team builds and reviews against.

  • Skills3 commands you type in Claude Code
  • Agents6 teammates a skill spawns
  • Standards2 rulebooks the team builds and reviews against

How a run flows

Your session is the team lead. It spawns the teammates, merges their findings, and decides the two gates. It never analyzes, builds, validates, or reviews anything itself.

  1. Mockup analysis
    • analyst
  2. UI development
    • developer
  3. QA, in parallel
    • visual-qa
    • behavior-qa
    • responsive-qa
  4. QA gateAll three pass on the same pass
  5. Final code review
    • code-reviewer
  6. Review gateNo Critical or High finding
  7. Ready for human reviewYou review the diff, commit, and open the PR

QA gate loop. Fails: the lead merges every finding into one fix list, the developer fixes, and all three QA engineers run again. Up to 3 QA passes.

Review gate loop. Critical or High findings: a fix round, the QA gate again, then a new review. Up to 3 review rounds.

Steps

  1. Mockup analysis. analyst writes the spec. If it reports blockers, the run is blocked; stop and report.
  2. UI development. developer builds every breakpoint from the spec and tells the three QA engineers it is ready.
  3. Visual QA, Behavior QA, and Responsive QA run in parallel on the same pass and each send a full verdict to the lead.
  4. Developer fixes. The lead merges the visual deltas, the behavior issues, and the responsive deltas into one fix list, tagged visual, behavior, or responsive, and creates a "Fix: pass N" task for developer. Only the lead sends findings to the developer, so the three QA streams never produce conflicting instructions.
  5. Revalidation. After every fix pass all three QA engineers run again from the full spec, not just the fixed items, because a fix at one width can move pixels at another and a visual fix can break a handler.
  6. Final code review. reviewer runs once all three QA verdicts have matches true. Critical and High findings go back to developer as a fix round, followed by full revalidation and a new review round. Medium and Low are advisory.

Gates and caps

  • QA gate passes when visual-qa, behavior-qa, and responsive-qa all report matches true with zero blocking items on the same pass. Cap: 3 QA passes (2 fix passes). At the cap the run is escalated at the QA gate.
  • Review gate passes when reviewer reports approved true. Cap: 3 review rounds. At the cap the run is escalated at the review gate.
  • Derived is not matched. A breakpoint with no frame is checked against section 8, and the report says "no design to compare" for it, never "matches".
  • Unverified is not passed. Anything any QA engineer lists under notChecked is reported as unverified with the reason. A run with unverified items is ready-for-human-review with unverified items, never complete. A static method is reported as weaker evidence than rendered.
  • Pixel-perfect is claimed only when the final visual deltas list is empty, including minor items. Otherwise the report lists every unmatched item, blocking first.

Skills

3

The commands you type in Claude Code. Each one turns the session into the team lead and follows its playbook.

Skill

/build-ui

Run the UI implementation agent team on a mockup.

Takes a Figma URL or a mockup image path plus a short description of what to build, optionally the mobile and tablet frames from their own Figma sections, and leads the team (analyst, developer, visual QA, behavior QA, responsive QA, code reviewer) through the QA gate and the code review gate.

  • Project mode: new
  • Run by you only
  • Leads 6 agents
/build-ui <figma-url | image-path> <what to build and where>
3 options
--mobile <figma-url | image-path>

The mobile frame of the same screen. Designers hand it over in its own Figma section, so it is never found from the desktop frame; it must be passed here. A Figma URL must include a node-id. An image path must exist.

Example/build-ui https://www.figma.com/design/AbC123/Shop?node-id=12-34 pricing page in build/pricing/ --mobile https://www.figma.com/design/AbC123/Shop?node-id=56-78
--tablet <figma-url | image-path>

The tablet frame, same rules.

Example/build-ui https://www.figma.com/design/AbC123/Shop?node-id=12-34 pricing page in build/pricing/ --tablet designs/pricing-tablet.png
--breakpoints <desktop>,<tablet>,<mobile>

Viewport widths in px. Default 1440,768,375. A Figma breakpoint source overrides its entry with the frame's real width once the analyst reports it.

Example/build-ui https://www.figma.com/design/AbC123/Shop?node-id=12-34 pricing page in build/pricing/ --breakpoints 1280,834,390

Skill

/convert-ui

Run the UI implementation agent team to convert a whole project prototype into the actual UI implementation.

Takes the folder of a downloaded prototype (for example a Claude Design export handed over by another team) and converts it page by page: every page in one run, or one page per run with --page. The basis of the output is uiux-development-standard.md; the prototype is the source of truth for the design and any functionality it has, so only the tech stack and the coding standard change. Same team and gates as /build-ui. Writes the converted UI to build/<name>/ and never edits the prototype. A single page file, a screenshot or other image, or a Figma URL is also accepted and converted as one screen.

  • Project mode: new
  • Run by you only
  • Follows /build-ui
  • Leads 6 agents
/convert-ui <prototype-folder | page-file | image-path | figma-url> [which pages to convert, default all]
2 options
--page <name>

Convert only this page in this run, and add it to what earlier runs already converted. The name is the page's name, file name, or route, matched without regard to case or extension. It can be given more than once, or as a comma-separated list. This is how a prototype is converted page by page across several runs.

Example/convert-ui prototypes/shop --page pricing,checkout
--keep-structure

Convert, but follow the prototype's existing structure of files and folders. The build keeps the same folders and the same file names as the prototype, and the standard's own folder layout is not imposed. Section 4 below says exactly what changes. Without this flag the build uses the structure the standard describes.

Example/convert-ui prototypes/shop --keep-structure

Skill

/update-ui

Run the UI implementation agent team on a mockup to update a page, section, or component inside an existing project.

Same team and gates as /build-ui, in project mode existing, so the project's own styling stack, token file, breakpoint approach, and folder structure are followed and no second structure is created. Takes a Figma URL or a mockup image path plus the existing file or directory to update.

  • Project mode: existing
  • Run by you only
  • Follows /build-ui
  • Leads 6 agents
/update-ui <figma-url | image-path> <what to update and in which existing file or directory>
3 options
--mobile <figma-url | image-path>

From /build-ui: the mobile frame of the same screen. Designers hand it over in its own Figma section, so it is never found from the desktop frame; it must be passed here. A Figma URL must include a node-id. An image path must exist.

Example/update-ui https://www.figma.com/design/AbC123/Shop?node-id=12-34 hero section in resources/js/pages/Pricing.vue --mobile https://www.figma.com/design/AbC123/Shop?node-id=56-78
--tablet <figma-url | image-path>

From /build-ui: the tablet frame, same rules.

Example/update-ui https://www.figma.com/design/AbC123/Shop?node-id=12-34 hero section in resources/js/pages/Pricing.vue --tablet designs/pricing-tablet.png
--breakpoints <desktop>,<tablet>,<mobile>

From /build-ui: viewport widths in px. Default 1440,768,375. A Figma breakpoint source overrides its entry with the frame's real width once the analyst reports it.

Example/update-ui https://www.figma.com/design/AbC123/Shop?node-id=12-34 hero section in resources/js/pages/Pricing.vue --breakpoints 1280,834,390
